data.narrative:
Calogena is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised €100M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 firms—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo—all operating in the same sector at comparable or adjacent funding stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for current valuation, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $200M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A), and Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B)—produces a median valuation of $808M, with a range of $200M to $6.0B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods implies a valuation range of $170M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $504M. The wide spread reflects meaningful heterogeneity within the nuclear energy peer set, particularly the outlier valuation of Valar Atomics. Key uncertainties center on stage-appropriate comparability—whether Series B valuations should anchor a Series A assessment—and the degree to which early-stage nuclear companies command sector-specific premiums independent of conventional biotech or hardware benchmarks.
